Analysis: Both hypotheses propose innovative mechanisms by which tumor cells subvert the immune system. Hypothesis 1 is novel in its proposal of a dual cargo system borne by EVs to deliver oncogenic miRNAs and cytokine modulators, a concept that leverages established effects of miRNAs (e.g., miR-21 and miR-155) while introducing the challenge of verifying cytokine incorporation. Its experimental plan—using single‐cell RNA sequencing and CRISPR screens—is robust, making it relatively straightforward to test key mechanistic components despite needing more evidence on dual packaging. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 is also conceptually appealing by linking tumor lactate metabolism to an emerging epigenetic modification (histone lactylation) in MDSCs. However, it currently suffers from a paucity of direct empirical evidence and mechanistic clarity regarding the enzymes responsible for lactylation, as well as the integration with the traditional GM‑CSF/STAT3 pathway. While both ideas incorporate advanced methodologies, Hypothesis 1 has a slightly stronger plausibility and testability profile given existing supporting frameworks for EV-mediated miRNA delivery. Safety considerations in both require further investigation, though Hypothesis 1’s strategies (using engineered EVs and miRNA antagonists) are built upon a more well-established foundation in cancer research.
